subject.title: fix(release): publish ClawHub bootstrap artifacts immutably

question: Do release owners approve this trusted-main immutable artifact handoff as the permanent security boundary for first-time ClawHub publication?
rationale: The patch fixes a real beta blocker but also defines which code may execute around the bootstrap credential and which exact official package bytes are authorized for publication.

options.title: Approve after final proof
options.body: Adopt the design after final-head evidence demonstrates artifact/run binding, validation before credential loading, exact-file publication, and byte-identical registry readback.

options.title: Request a narrower boundary
options.body: Reduce the workflow or manifest surface if release owners cannot confidently audit and operate the current design.

options.title: Keep bootstrap manual
options.body: Use a controlled manual first-publish process until the automated boundary is proven and accepted.

recommendation.title: Approve after final proof
recommendation.body: Adopt the design after final-head evidence demonstrates artifact/run binding, validation before credential loading, exact-file publication, and byte-identical registry readback.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the canonical blocker and current implementation, with Patrick-Erichsen and steipete as strong adjacent review candidates.
